reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected SEC exhibit rows shows a stronger GAAP earnings profile alongside a weaker credit-loss trajectory. Net interest income, noninterest income, pretax income and net income all rose sequentially, and the credit-loss provision was lower, while total noninterest expense was slightly lower on reduced merger-related expense; the company-defined adjusted net income also rose. Offsetting this, the allowance for credit losses and its coverage of loans declined, and both the reported annualized net charge-off ratio and the company-defined net charge-off ratio excluding acquisition-date effects rose, with the exclusion-adjusted ratio converging on the reported ratio. Total nonperforming assets and the nonperforming-asset ratio were essentially unchanged, and non-acquired nonperforming assets were roughly flat while acquired nonperforming assets declined. The lower provision is therefore not corroborated by improving charge-off or coverage indicators, and the selected rows do not establish whether the provision decline reflects reserve release, portfolio mix, acquisition accounting effects, or a lag in loss recognition. The thesis requires the full set of listed event metrics, and the selected extract does not supply a comparable acquisition-date charge-off figure for the event quarter, so the credit-quality picture cannot be closed on this evidence. Because the selected evidence supports a defensible but incomplete view, the research state is held for review rather than upgraded or invalidated; conviction and status are preserved and no trade is implied.
